claims.text: Arthrocentesis for a new effusion, to exclude infection and identify crystals.
claims.quote: Arthrocentesis is mandatory in most patients with a new effusion to exclude infection and identify crystals

claims.text: Synovial fluid: WBC count with differential, Gram stain and cultures, and polarized-light microscopy for crystals.
claims.quote: Synovial fluid examination includes white blood cell (WBC) count with differential, Gram stain and cultures, and microscopic examination for crystals using polarized light.

claims.text: Crystals confirm crystal-induced arthritis but do not exclude a coexisting infection.
claims.quote: Finding crystals in synovial fluid confirms crystal-induced arthritis but does not exclude coexisting infection.

claims.text: ESR and CRP suggest inflammation but are nonspecific, particularly in older adults.
claims.quote: Elevated ESR and CRP levels suggest inflammation but are nonspecific, particularly in older adults.

claims.text: Serologies (ANA, double-stranded DNA, rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP, ANCA) once a systemic inflammatory disorder is clinically suspected.
claims.quote: Once a diagnosis of a systemic inflammatory disorder is clinically suspected, supportive serologic testing for antinuclear antibodies, double-stranded DNA, rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) may assist in making the diagnosis.

claims.text: Serum urate does not diagnose gout: it is neither sensitive nor specific.
claims.quote: Serum urate level should not be used to diagnose gout because it is neither sensitive nor specific

claims.text: X-rays and/or ultrasound in chronic arthritis, looking for joint damage such as erosions in rheumatoid arthritis.
claims.quote: If arthritis is chronic, radiographs and/or ultrasound are typically done to look for signs of joint damage (eg, erosions in rheumatoid arthritis).

claims.text: In acute monarthritis x-rays rarely change the diagnosis unless fracture or osteomyelitis is suspected.
claims.quote: Radiographs rarely change the diagnosis in acute monarthritis unless fracture or osteomyelitis is suspected.
